question: Gandhiji gave a call for a satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act in which of the following years?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** gave a call for **Satyagraha** against the **Rowlatt Act** in the year **1919**. This act was officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the **British Government** to curb revolutionary activities in India. It allowed the government to arrest and detain individuals without trial for two years. This was seen as a suppression of civil liberties.
 
• The call for **Satyagraha** by Gandhi was a nonviolent resistance against the oppressive policies of the British, particularly the Rowlatt Act. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The nationwide Satyagraha, also known as the **Rowlatt Satyagraha**, marked the first all-India struggle against British rule under Gandhi's leadership.
 
• The movement witnessed widespread protests, hartals (strikes), and public meetings. However, it also led to violent clashes in some regions, which Gandhi strongly condemned, emphasizing his commitment to nonviolence.
 
• The infamous **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** occurred on **13 April 1919** in Amritsar during the same period, further fueling anti-British sentiments across India.
 
• The Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act is considered a precursor to the larger national movements for India's independence. *Hence, the correct answer is 1919.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**

 
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in **March 1919**. It was designed to curb the growing nationalist and revolutionary activities in India.
 
• This act allowed the government to suppress publications, arrest individuals without a warrant, and detain them without trial, violating basic civil liberties and judicial rights.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha Movement:**
 
 
• The Satyagraha movement marked the adoption of nonviolent methods of resistance by **Mahatma Gandhi** on a nationwide scale.
 
• The philosophy of Satyagraha was based on the principles of **truth, nonviolence, and civil disobedience**. It emphasized the moral strength of the people.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Rowlatt Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha led to widespread protests and demonstrations, uniting Indians from different regions, religions, and communities against British rule.
 
• Although the Satyagraha was eventually withdrawn due to outbreaks of violence, it played a crucial role in laying the foundation for future mass movements like the **Non-Cooperation Movement** (1920).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• The massacre occurred on **13 April 1919** in **Amritsar**, Punjab. General **Reginald Dyer** ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering, killing hundreds of men, women, and children.
 
• This tragic event intensified the public's anger against British rule and strengthened the demand for self-rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi's Leadership:**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first major movement led by Gandhi after his return to India in **1915**. It established him as a key leader in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• Gandhi's emphasis on nonviolence became the guiding principle of the freedom struggle in the years to come.
